land.text: Ruanda, the northern half of the Belgian-administered Ruanda-Urundi: 'Part of Ruanda-Urundi: 1916–1962'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Ruanda-Urundi inside its Belgian Congo shape; the belgian-congo dossier carries the 1 July 1962 loss. The older Kingdom of Rwanda (kingdom-of-rwanda, to 1897) is the same land before the German and Belgian period. The republic was declared on 28 January 1961 under Belgian administration, before sovereignty.

capitals.name: Kigali
capitals.note: 'Its capital and largest city is Kigali.' The page gives no date for the seat and does not mention Nyanza or Butare, so 'from' is the start year.

correction.text: Rwanda as it stands in Cliopatria's 1963 shape, applied from independence: 'gained independence on 1 July 1962'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1963 but independence was 1 July 1962 (infobox 'Independence from Belgium: 1 July 1962'; 'Republic declared: 28 January 1961', which was under Belgian trusteeship). The land is the 1963 shape unchanged.

25,419 km2 against the infobox 26,338 km2 total (6.3 percent water, about 24,680 km2 of land): ratio 0.97 of the total, 1.03 of the land. The page describes no border change or territorial dispute since independence ('bordered by Uganda to the north, Tanzania to the east, Burundi to the south, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west'), so one shape holds for 1963-2023. The Rwandan armies' stays in the DR Congo are ledger occupations, not changes to this shape.
Same outline and area (25,419 km2) as 1963-2023; nothing on the page changes Rwanda's territory in 2024.

region.text: Rwanda: 'gained independence on 1 July 1962'; infobox 'Part of Ruanda-Urundi: 1916–1962'

ledger.note: 1 July 1962: Rwanda becomes independent of Belgium, already a republic. Infobox 'Independence from Belgium: 1 July 1962'; 'Republic declared: 28 January 1961'; 'In 1961, the suddenly pro-Hutu Belgians held a referendum in which the country voted to abolish the monarchy.' The page names the country, not a boundary.

region.text: the Kivus: 'The RCD quickly took control of the towns of Bukavu and Uvira in the Kivus'; the RCD 'based its operations in Goma'

ledger.note: August 1998: the Second Congo War opens and Rwanda holds the Kivus. 'It began on 2 August 1998'; 'The Tutsi-led Rwandan government allied with Uganda'; the RCD 'quickly came to dominate the resource-rich eastern provinces'. The page does not call Rwanda's presence an occupation or draw its zone: the Kivus are the researcher's reading of Bukavu, Uvira and Goma; the Rwanda article calls the RPF-led army 'a key belligerent in the First and Second Congo Wars'.

region.text: Kisangani, 'the diamond center', where the Ugandan and Rwandan armies clashed

ledger.note: 7 August 1999: the Rwandan and Ugandan armies fight in Kisangani. 'Tensions between Uganda and Rwanda escalated as units of the Uganda People's Defense Force and the Rwandan Patriotic Army clashed in Kisangani on the morning of 7 August'; the page's section is 1999.

region.text: Kisangani, 'the diamond center', where the Ugandan and Rwandan armies clashed

ledger.note: 17 August 1999: a ceasefire halts the first Kisangani fighting. 'The conflict lasted until 17 August, when a ceasefire was called that day.'

region.text: Kisangani, 'the diamond center', where the Ugandan and Rwandan armies clashed

ledger.note: May 2000: Rwanda and Uganda fight again in Kisangani. The page: 'heavy fighting between Uganda and Rwanda in Kisangani in May and June 2000'.

region.text: Kisangani, 'the diamond center', where the Ugandan and Rwandan armies clashed

ledger.note: June 2000: the second Kisangani fighting ends (the page says only 'in May and June 2000'; June is the last month it names).

region.text: the Kivus: 'The RCD quickly took control of the towns of Bukavu and Uvira in the Kivus'; the RCD 'based its operations in Goma'

ledger.note: 5 October 2002: Rwanda announces the end of its withdrawal from the DR Congo. 'On 5 October Rwanda announced the completion of its withdrawal' and 'MONUC confirmed the departure of over 20,000 Rwandan soldiers', after the Pretoria Accord of 30 July 2002; the year is that of the section the sentence stands in. The RCD-Goma remained in Goma until the war ended on 18 July 2003.

wars.name: Rwandan Civil War
wars.outcome: The RPF 'invaded northern Rwanda from their base in Uganda' in 1990; after the genocide began on 6 April 1994 'the RPF ended the genocide with a military victory in July 1994'. No border changed.
wars.note: The page dates no RPF-held zone, so none is mapped (rule 5 needs a land and a date); a rebel dossier for the RPF-held north would need a page that gives its extent.

wars.name: Second Congo War

zones.text: the Kivus: 'The RCD quickly took control of the towns of Bukavu and Uvira in the Kivus'; the RCD 'based its operations in Goma'

wars.outcome: Rwanda signed the Pretoria Accord with the DR Congo on 30 July 2002 and completed its withdrawal on 5 October 2002; the war 'officially ended on 18 July 2003 with the establishment of the Transitional Government'.
wars.note: The page offers no map text: the Kivus are named for the RCD's capture of Bukavu and Uvira. Rwanda and Uganda split in 1999 and fought in Kisangani on 7-17 August 1999 and in May-June 2000.

certainty.note: Inherited Ruanda-Urundi boundaries 'broken up along traditional lines' in 1962; the page records no change or dispute since. Lake Kivu 'along most of the length of Rwanda's western border' is a natural line.

sources.title: Second Congo War
sources.note: The Second Congo War: Rwanda in the Kivus, the Kisangani clashes of 1999 and 2000, the Pretoria Accord and the withdrawal of October 2002.

notes: Cliopatria's Rwanda shape is the modern country (seed Seshat id rw_rwanda_rep); no border change since independence on the page, so the dossier adds the 1962 start (new keyframe) and the Congo-war stays. The ruler strip is omitted (no list on the page, 1-2 page budget). The 1961 republic is not an event because it predates the sovereign state (1 July 1962). The First Congo War (1996-97), in which the Rwandan army also fought in Zaire, was not opened (page budget): the DR Congo / Zaire dossiers and a gap-filler should add Rwanda's 1996-97 stay. The occupation events follow the occupier's side (counterpart = the owner); the DR Congo dossier should record the reverse.
